q: In Leviticus, why does God tell Israel to be holy?
why: God's people should be like Him.
quote: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

q: In Leviticus, God commands, “Love your neighbor as…”
quote: but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

q: In Leviticus, for whom should farmers leave grapes and the edges of the harvest?
quote: Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.

q: In Leviticus, what should you do in the presence of the elderly?
why: Respect the aged and fear God.
quote: You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God.

q: In Leviticus, God says you must not steal and must not do what?
quote: You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another.

q: In Leviticus, what was to be kept burning on the altar continually?
quote: The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.

q: In Leviticus, what does God promise if Israel obeys?
quote: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.

q: In Leviticus, from where did the LORD call to Moses?
quote: Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting

q: In Leviticus, on whose head did Moses pour the anointing oil?
why: To set him apart as priest.
quote: He also poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.

q: In Leviticus, which of Aaron's sons offered unauthorized fire?
quote: Now Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers

q: In Leviticus, on the Day of Atonement, onto what were Israel's sins confessed?
why: It was sent into the wilderness.
quote: Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities

q: In Leviticus, where was the goat carrying Israel's sins sent?
why: It carried their sins far away.
quote: The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place

q: In Leviticus, what is the seventh day called?
quote: but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest

q: In Leviticus, what was the fiftieth year called?
why: Liberty was proclaimed in the land.
quote: It shall be your Jubilee

q: In Leviticus, to whom does the tithe of the land belong?
why: It is holy to the LORD.
quote: Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD

q: In Leviticus' food laws, which animals could Israel eat?
quote: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.

q: In Leviticus, what had to be added to every grain offering?
why: It is the salt of the covenant.
quote: And you shall season each of your grain offerings with salt.

q: In Leviticus, what was the second goat of the Day of Atonement called?
why: Lots were cast for the two goats.
quote: one for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat

q: In Leviticus, on which day of the seventh month was the Day of Atonement?
quote: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any work

q: In Leviticus, on which day of the first month does Passover begin?
quote: The Passover to the LORD begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.

q: In Leviticus, how many days does the Feast of Tabernacles last?
why: It begins on the fifteenth of the seventh month.
quote: the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD begins, and it continues for seven days.

q: In Leviticus, how many days were counted to the offering of new grain?
quote: You shall count off fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath

q: In Leviticus, where does God say the life of the flesh is?
quote: For the life of the flesh is in the blood

q: In Leviticus, where did God appear above the ark?
a: In the cloud over the mercy seat
quote: because I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
